reference_drawer.title: 📖 Nature of Roots Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Rules for classifying roots and determining parameter conditions from the discriminant.

items.rule: For ax²+bx+c=0, D=b²−4ac determines the nature of the roots.
items.formula: \begin{aligned}D &> 0 \implies \text{two distinct real roots} \\ D &= 0 \implies \text{two equal real roots} \\ D &< 0 \implies \text{no real roots}\end{aligned}
items.example: D=25 gives distinct real roots; D=-4 gives no real roots.

items.rule: Real and equal roots require D=0.
items.example: Use this to determine an unknown parameter.
The boundary D=0 gives equal roots.

items.rule: Two distinct real roots require D>0.
No real roots occur when D<0.
items.example: Use a strict inequality for parameter ranges.

concepts.title: 1. Classification of Roots
concepts.subtitle: Connect D with root nature
concepts.summary: For ax²+bx+c=0, the sign of D=b²−4ac classifies the roots without finding them.

points.text: D > 0 gives two distinct real roots.
D = 0 gives two equal real roots.

concepts.trap: Using D≥0 when the question specifically asks for distinct roots.

concepts.title: 2. Equal Roots Condition
concepts.subtitle: Use D=0 to determine k
concepts.summary: Real and equal roots occur exactly when the discriminant is zero. Parameter questions therefore become equations in k.

points.text: Set D=0 and solve for k.

concepts.trap: Stopping at D=0 instead of solving the resulting equation.

concepts.title: 3. Parameter and Range Conditions
concepts.subtitle: Translate root nature into inequalities
concepts.summary: Distinct real roots require D>0, while no real roots require D<0. These become parameter inequalities.

points.text: Write D as a function of k.
Solve k and exclude the boundary.

concepts.trap: Including the boundary value in a strict range.

concepts.title: 4. Real-Root Conditions in Algebraic Contexts
concepts.subtitle: Check root existence without solving
concepts.summary: For real roots, D must be non-negative. For distinct roots, D must be positive. Equal roots require D=0.

points.text: Compare D with the required threshold.

concepts.trap: Using the constant term or another coefficient as the root test.

concepts.title: 5. Parameter Interpretation
concepts.subtitle: Understand boundaries and ranges
concepts.summary: The value where D=0 is the boundary between different root-nature regions. Strict inequalities exclude that boundary.

points.text: Test the requested side of the boundary.

concepts.trap: Confusing the D=0 boundary with the full range for distinct or non-real roots.
